Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we scope the 8-week pilot: our usage shows a risk of 2x spikes during internal stress tests. The team would prefer not to commit to a large prepaid credit bucket up-front. Can Redwood do a short addendum that formalizes an insurance-style coverage (flat fee + capped overage) instead of prepay credits? Also curious how SKU rebalancing would work — we could move some endpoints to a cheaper quantized variant during bursts if that helps.

Attached a short usage snapshot and our test schedule.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

—Anna

Subject: Re: Pilot runway question — surge handling and cost buffer

Hi Anna — great context and thanks for the attachment.

Short answer: yes, we can do both patterns. Two practical options we typically propose for pilots: 

1) Surge insurance (flat fee + capped overage) — you pay a small non-refundable fee that reserves burst capacity for the pilot window. This covers a pre-agreed N token-hours of burst; after that a reduced overage rate applies (we can cap monthly overage to X% of the pilot commit).

2) Credit-based runway + dynamic SKU rebalance — smaller prepaid credit bucket for baseline, with automatic routing to quantized/cheaper model variants during defined burst windows to keep latency acceptable and cost lower.

Pros/cons at a glance:
- Insurance: predictable bill, minimal procurement friction (one fee), good for teams that want cost certainty for bursts.
- Credits + rebalance: lower flat cost, engineering needs to accept potential quality delta during bursts unless we pin routes to higher-quality models.

Questions for sizing a proposal:
- What is the expected peak burst duration in token-hours? (your sheet has a few scenarios but we need a 95th percentile estimate)
- Would your compliance team accept temporary quantized model routing for non-prod tests?

I can draft a 1-page addendum with either option. If you want, I can include a hybrid: small insurance fee that covers the first X bursts, plus a modest credit pool for sustained usage.

If you give me a target 95th percentile token-hours and a procurement contact, I can run numbers and send an addendum.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
